newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LAW, MOODY RECALLED FOR ONE-DAY MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LAW, MOODY RECALLED FOR ONE-DAY MATCHES.

text.p: Australia selectors on Tuesday recalled all-rounders Stuart Law and Tom Moody for the first two limited overs matches against West Indies this week.
Law and Moody replace opening batsman Matthew Elliott and pace bowler Michael Kasprowicz in the 12-man squad for the matches in Melbourne on Friday and Sydney on Sunday.

Elliott was injured in a mid-pitch collision on Monday with batting partner Mark Waugh during the second test against West Indies and was due to undergo surgery to repair cartilage damage in his right knee later on Tuesday.
Kasprowicz was used only sparingly and did not take a wicket in the second test, won by 124 runs by Australia on Tuesday.
Moody, captain of Worcestershire in English county cricket, last played for Australia against West Indies in the 1992/93 season.
He steered his Western Australia state side to a win over South Australia in a Sheffield Shield match on Monday with an innings 89 not out.
Law was dropped after Australia's unsuccessful short tour of India last month.
Pace bowler Paul Reiffel, who missed the second test with a neck strain, also returns.
Pakistan arrive next week to take part in the triangular limited overs series.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Ian Healy, Michael Bevan, Greg Blewett, Jason Gillespie, Stuart Law, Glenn McGrath, Tom Moody, Ricky Ponting, Paul Reiffel, Shane Warne, Mark Waugh.
